questions.q: In the worked example's relational schema, what role does the `OrderItems` table play?
options: A junction table resolving the many-to-many relationship between Orders and Products
The primary table storing customer information
A lookup table for product categories
An audit log of schema changes
questions.explain: OrderItems connects Orders and Products, holding Quantity as the data specific to that particular pairing.

questions.q: Why do Customers, Products, and Orders each become their own node in the graph model?
options: Each has independent identity, is referenced from multiple places, and is a natural thing to query directly
Because every table in a relational schema must become a node
Because they were the largest tables in the schema
Because they contain foreign keys
questions.explain: This follows the node-or-property test from the previous lesson — shared, independently-queried entities become nodes.

questions.q: What does `OrderItems` become in the resulting graph model, and why?
options: A CONTAINS relationship between Order and Product, because a junction table's job is connecting two other tables
Its own OrderItem node, connected to both Order and Product
A property directly on the Customer node
It is dropped entirely and its data is lost
questions.explain: A junction table whose only purpose is connecting two entities and carrying pairing-specific data maps onto a relationship, not a separate node.

questions.q: Where does the `Quantity` column end up in the graph model?
options: As a property on the CONTAINS relationship between Order and Product
As a new node called Quantity
As a property on the Customer node
It has no equivalent in the graph model
questions.explain: Since a relationship can carry its own properties, Quantity — data specific to that Order/Product pairing — lives directly on the CONTAINS relationship.

questions.q: What happens to the foreign key columns (like Orders.CustomerId) when converting to the graph model?
options: They become relationships (e.g. a PLACED relationship from Customer to Order), not properties
They are kept as properties on the Order node exactly as before
They are deleted with no replacement
They are converted into node labels
questions.explain: The general pattern is foreign key becomes relationship — Orders.CustomerId becomes a PLACED relationship connecting the two nodes directly.
